PullRequest.Title: Enforce managed plugin enablement in the model and UI
PullRequest.Body:
Part of: https://github.com/microsoft/vscode-internalbacklog/issues/8906

- Apply managed `enabledPlugins` `true` and `false` entries as an immutable overlay on VS Code's plugin enablement model.
- Keep the user's profile and workspace choice stored underneath policy, restoring it when the managed entry is removed.
- Ignore local enablement writes and removal-state cleanup for managed identities.
- Give a policy-required plugin priority over unmanaged duplicates in the same collision group.
- Lock managed switches and enablement actions, and hide uninstall for policy-required plugins across every existing plugin management surface.
- Leave policy-omitted plugins user-controlled, preserving additive behavior rather than turning `enabledPlugins` into an allowlist.

## Reproduction

Using an isolated Code OSS profile, fixture plugins, and a temporary `ChatEnabledPlugins` policy:

- `required-demo@repro-8906-local: true`
- `blocked-demo@repro-8906-local: false`
- `unmanaged-demo`: omitted from policy

Before this change, `blocked-demo` was disabled and locked, proving the policy was active. `required-demo` remained user-toggleable; disabling it removed its contributed skill and persisted a local `false` decision while policy still required it.

Reproduction details: https://github.com/microsoft/vscode-internalbacklog/issues/8906#issuecomment-5771771859

## Verification

The same isolated scenario was replayed with `required-demo` pre-seeded as locally disabled:

- `required-demo` stayed checked and locked by managed `true`.
- `blocked-demo` stayed unchecked and locked by managed `false`.
- `unmanaged-demo` remained enabled and user-toggleable.
- The fixture skill count remained `2`, confirming required and unmanaged contributions were active.
- The stored local `false` decision remained unchanged underneath the effective managed `true`.

A clean negative control applied the managed-precedence behavior test to the unmodified base; it failed on the expected policy assertion.

## Scope

- This PR enforces effective enablement and user controls for plugins that are already discovered.
- Managed acquisition and restoration of a missing plugin are handled separately by #337221.
- Fail-closed behavior when a required plugin cannot be resolved remains a product decision.
- This does not change Agent Host wire contracts or runtime-owned enforcement.

-----------------------------------------
Inspirations from:

- Managed `true`/`false` and additive semantics come from [`ChatConfiguration.EnabledPlugins`](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/blob/62c8ac8ac5e0feaba1fa728fa48b10403f96ccab/src/vs/workbench/contrib/chat/browser/chat.shared.contribution.ts#L1365-L1372).
- Collision ordering and transactional updates preserve the behavior of [`CollisionEnablementModel`](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/blob/62c8ac8ac5e0feaba1fa728fa48b10403f96ccab/src/vs/workbench/contrib/chat/common/enablement.ts#L174-L235).
- The existing managed identity and explicit `true` interpretation are already used by [managed-only hook filtering](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/blob/62c8ac8ac5e0feaba1fa728fa48b10403f96ccab/src/vs/workbench/contrib/chat/common/promptSyntax/service/promptsServiceImpl.ts#L1432-L1439).

Scenarios.Scenario: Workbench startup and plugin discovery with managed enablement policy applied
Scenarios.CriticalPath: The four registered discovery sources start independently; each source must finish its existing discovery work before the combined plugin list becomes available. The added policy overlay runs synchronously only after discovery/config observables publish and performs in-memory map construction; it adds no filesystem or network wait to discovery.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Resolve plugin directories, detect formats, read manifests/components, and establish file watchers during discovery.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Existing per discovered source/plugin, deduplicated by URI within each discovery refresh; the PR adds no calls.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same discovery sources performed the same filesystem operations before the diff.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: These existing operations gate each discovery source's publication. The added policy map executes only after those publications and does not add another boundary call.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Read the effective ChatEnabledPlugins policy from the configuration service when the relevant configuration event fires.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One inspection per relevant configuration event, unchanged by the diff; the resulting value serves all plugins.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same observable and configuration inspection already drove policy-blocked handling.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: The inspection feeds existing and new in-memory derived state but is not multiplied per plugin.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Total unique discovered plugins across configured, marketplace, extension, and Copilot CLI sources. The new policy map is O(P) per discovery or policy invalidation, after source-level deduplication; collision grouping was already collection-wide.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Discovery schedulers can run independently across the four sources, while each source's per-plugin filesystem operations are awaited serially. Observable recomputation and the policy transaction are synchronous and coalesced by derived-observable caching/transactions; there is no new concurrency burst.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Existing plugin entries are reused by URI across refreshes. The new derived policy map is cached while observed and invalidated only by discovery-list or policy changes; it is not rebuilt for every per-plugin reactive read. No negative-cache behavior changes.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: the diff and observable implementation show one cached collection scan per invalidation, with no newly introduced boundary operations.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: No benchmark quantifies the additional O(P) map allocation, but plugin collections are bounded by discovered installations and the work occurs on infrequent discovery/policy invalidations, not input/render loops.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression. The added O(P) in-memory policy-map pass is bounded, cached while observed, and small relative to the pre-existing discovery and collision-group passes.

Scenarios.Scenario: Open or update the plugin list, embedded detail, or plugin editor while policy state changes
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Visible row/detail/editor autoruns synchronously read per-plugin enablement and policy observables and update a switch, action bar, or detail DOM. The virtualized list limits row work to rendered entries; a policy change updates managed plugins transactionally.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Load an installed plugin README when opening details.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: At most one cached README request for the selected editor item; unchanged by the policy-action diff.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Opening plugin details already loaded the selected plugin README.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: README loading is on the existing detail-open path, but the new policy observable read neither triggers nor multiplies it.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Use existing marketplace data/fetch state when rendering plugin editor/list metadata and actions.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Existing list/editor refresh behavior, grouped by the marketplace service rather than per policy check.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Marketplace fetching and cached snapshots already existed on these surfaces.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Policy reads are local and do not initiate marketplace requests.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Rendered plugin rows plus any open detail/editor panes. Per rendered item, the diff adds constant-time observable reads and DOM property updates; full detail rerender occurs only when that selected plugin's policy value changes.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: UI updates run synchronously on the renderer thread through observable transactions. There is no subprocess, IPC, filesystem, database, or network work introduced by the policy checks, and no asynchronous fan-out.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Per-plugin policy observables hold the current tri-state value. Global policy lookup is served from the observed derived map; list virtualization and disposable stores bound active row subscriptions to rendered UI lifetime.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: changed UI hunks only add observable reads, action replacement, and bounded DOM state updates; transitive detail/marketplace boundaries remain unchanged.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Exact visible-row counts and policy-update frequency vary, but the changed work is constant per rendered row and policy updates are administrative rather than frame-rate events.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression. The UI work is bounded by visible/rendered items and no changed line adds layout reads, network/filesystem calls, or long-lived unbounded state.

Scenarios.Scenario: User toggles plugin enablement or invokes a managed plugin action
Scenarios.CriticalPath: For unmanaged plugins, a click performs the existing enablement-model write and now immediately reads the effective in-memory state before updating the switch. For managed plugins, the handler exits before persistence; managed actions only show a notification.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Persist profile/workspace plugin enablement through ObservableMemento/storage when an unmanaged toggle is accepted.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One logical toggle update, plus existing updates for duplicate collision members; unchanged for unmanaged plugins and eliminated for managed plugins.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Unmanaged toggles already called setEnabled and persisted the same enablement state.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: The added post-write read is in-memory and does not add another storage write. Managed policy checks return before the storage boundary.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: One selected plugin and, only when enabling a collision member, that plugin's collision group. The added policy check is O(1) map lookup; collision-group scanning remains bounded to duplicate identities.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: A single synchronous user action runs at a time. Collision updates use one transaction; there is no parallel I/O or burst scheduling.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: The policy map is cached while plugin enablement is observed. The base enablement maps remain the authoritative persisted state, preserving the existing storage lifecycle; rejected managed writes do not mutate or invalidate storage.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: the call path shows the only added operation after setEnabled is readEnabled, while managed paths avoid the existing persistence boundary.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Collision-group size depends on duplicate installations, but effective cardinality is the duplicate group rather than the full plugin collection and is normally small.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression. The diff neither increases storage-call cardinality nor introduces a hot synchronous workload.

Analysis.Summary: Completed the performance pass over all 10 changed files and traced startup discovery, policy invalidation, UI rendering, editor/detail opening, and enablement writes. The diff adds bounded cached map/observable work and constant-time UI checks, with no new expensive boundary, fan-out, leak, or hot-path synchronous regression.

Stats.CostNote: Copilot SDK reports nano-AI units and model billing multipliers; it does not provide a USD conversion.
